title: Bell X-1
summary: The Bell X-1 was the rocket-powered aircraft that first flew faster than the speed of sound in 1947.
description: The Bell X-1, named Glamorous Glennis by pilot Chuck Yeager, became the first airplane to fly faster than the speed of sound on October 14, 1947. It was air-launched from a Boeing B-29 and reached Mach 1.06, about 700 miles per hour, over the Mojave Desert near Muroc Dry Lake, California. The flight proved that the so-called sound barrier could be crossed by a carefully designed aircraft. The X-1 was developed through a cooperative program involving NACA, the U.S. Army Air Forces, and Bell Aircraft Corporation. Its bullet-like shape, rocket engine, pressurized cockpit, propellant tanks, and flight-test instruments made it a compact research aircraft built for transonic and supersonic experiments. The aircraft later reached Mach 1.45 and helped open the era of practical supersonic flight. In this exhibition, the Bell X-1 can be explained as a milestone where engineering, risk, test piloting, and scientific measurement changed the future of aviation.
sourceInstitution: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
